literal: His wording ran: "Once a hundred thousand rode rampant; General Fan begged and was humbled;
idiomatic: His lines read: "Once a hundred thousand swept the land; Fan the general begged and bowed;

literal: Five thousand pushed deep; Commandant Li surrendered and did not return.
idiomatic: Five thousand went deep; Commandant Li surrendered and never came back.

literal: " At the time they prized his craft.
idiomatic: " People then prized his skill.

literal: Later the court made many transfers and dismissals, with investitures urged on the same day.
idiomatic: Later the court shuffled many posts and urged same-day appointments.

literal: Xun Zu stood outside the East Stop-Carriage Gate and drafted memorials for more than twenty men without adding a dot; the wording was sound.
idiomatic: Xun Zu stood at the East Stop-Carriage Gate and wrote twenty-odd memorials at a stroke, all clear and polished.

literal: When Xun Zu first inherited the title, an elder statesman said, "Great Xia is newly built"; Xun Zu answered at once, "At least the sparrows and swallows may congratulate."
idiomatic: On first inheriting the marquisate, an elder said, "Great Xia is newly built"; Xun Zu shot back, "At least sparrows and swallows can congratulate."

literal: At the end of Tianbao he was deputy commissioner for building the Long Wall.
idiomatic: Late in Tianbao he was deputy commissioner for the Long Wall.

literal: Confident in his talent yet inwardly resentful, he ruined his dress and appeared like a menial to see Yang Yin.
idiomatic: Sure of his gifts but inwardly bitter, he dressed like a laborer to see Yang Yin.

literal: Yin said: "Old friends all have some tie; only Great Xia has not yet been dealt with."
idiomatic: Yin said, "Old friends all have some hold on us—only Great Xia has not been handled."

literal: " Xun Zu said sharply, "Whose fault is that?"
idiomatic: " Xun Zu snapped, "Whose fault is that?"

literal: Once he reached the labor site he wrote "Fu on Building the Long Wall" to lodge his feelings.
idiomatic: At the work site he wrote a "Fu on Building the Long Wall" to vent his mood.

literal: In outline it runs: "Planks are purple cypress, pestles are papaya—who expected such timber for this use?
idiomatic: It says in part, "Planks of purple cypress, pestles of papaya—who thought such wood for this job?

literal: Grass spreads lush along the ridges and takes root.
idiomatic: Grass grows thick along the hills.

literal: If only every ten paces held one fragrant plant, I too would not mind dwelling among thorns."
idiomatic: If every ten paces had a fragrant blade, I would not mind living among thorns."

literal: Xing Shao often jested: "You are young yet your learning overflows; horned beasts have no upper teeth—I fear you will not live long."
idiomatic: Xing Shao teased him: "Young as you are, your learning overflows; horned beasts lack upper teeth—I fear you will die young."

literal: " He answered: "When Xun Zu first heard this I truly felt fear;
idiomatic: " He replied, "At first I was afraid;

literal: seeing my elder's temples already gray, I took some comfort."
idiomatic: but seeing your gray temples, I felt easier."

literal: " Shao greatly valued his quick wit.
idiomatic: " Shao prized his sharp tongue.

literal: He had eloquence and loved to praise or blame people.
idiomatic: Eloquent, he loved judging others.

literal: All envied him, saying he had relations with a cousin.
idiomatic: Many envied him, claiming an affair with a cousin.

literal: Clansman Simiao said to him: "Great Xia, why invite talk from the four seas?"
idiomatic: Kinsman Simiao asked, "Great Xia, why draw gossip from all under heaven?"

literal: " Xun Zu said: "Flesh and bone still tear at each other—how much more the ten thousand states bearing jade and silk."
idiomatic: " Xun Zu said, "Kin still tear each other apart—what of ten thousand states bearing tribute?"

literal: " He and Simiao were both northern talents; Wei Shou praised Simiao and held Xun Zu inferior.
idiomatic: He and Simiao were northern stars; Wei Shou praised Simiao and ranked Xun Zu below.

literal: Xun Zu told people: "Those who see one unable to soar high borrow his feathers;
idiomatic: Xun Zu said, "Those who see one who cannot fly high borrow his feathers;

literal: those who know one whose momentum will pierce the sky clip his wings."
idiomatic: those who know one destined to soar cut his pinions."

literal: As slander mounted day by day, common opinion all slighted his conduct.
idiomatic: Slander piled up daily and opinion turned against him.

literal: Changguang prefect Xing Ziguang said: "Xun Zu has Mi Heng's standards; Simiao lacks Kong Rong's edge."
idiomatic: Prefect Xing Ziguang said, "Xun Zu has Mi Heng's discipline; Simiao lacks Kong Rong's bite."

literal: Later he somewhat restrained himself.
idiomatic: Later he curbed himself somewhat.

literal: He served as Crown Prince Attendant and Secretariat Recorder, then died.
idiomatic: He was Crown Prince Attendant and Secretariat Recorder, then died.

literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls, all lost.
idiomatic: Ten scrolls of writings survive only by report.

literal: Gongdao's younger brother Huaidao was light and fond of wine, with considerable ambition.
idiomatic: Gongdao's brother Huaidao was reckless and fond of wine, yet ambitious.

literal: Since his house took part in the righteous rising, Shenwu treated him with personal favor.
idiomatic: His house had joined the righteous rising and Shenwu favored him personally.

literal: He died as garrison commander of Wusu.
idiomatic: He died as Wusu garrison commander.

literal: Huaidao's younger brother Zongdao was coarse and rash, given to wild gallantry, and held the post of southern Yingzhou inspector.
idiomatic: Brother Zongdao was rough and brash, a wild gallant, and southern Yingzhou inspector.

literal: Once at Jinyang he set out wine and guests filled the hall;
idiomatic: Once in Jinyang he held a feast and the hall was full;

literal: Palace Attendant Ma Shida eyed his konghou girl and said her hands were very fine; Zongdao at once gave her to him.
idiomatic: Attendant Ma Shida admired his konghou player's slender hands; Zongdao gave her to him at once.

literal: Shida firmly declined; Zongdao ordered his household to cut off her wrist, and Shida had no choice but to accept.
idiomatic: Shida refused; Zongdao ordered her wrist cut; Shida had to accept.

literal: About to go to Yingzhou, at Dugu Slope he gathered the township, slaughtered oxen, and held a feast.
idiomatic: Before leaving for Yingzhou he feasted the township at Dugu Slope with slaughtered oxen.

literal: An old retainer, drunk, spoke loosely; Zongdao had him drowned.
idiomatic: A drunken old retainer misspoke; Zongdao had him drowned.

literal: Later for cruel excess he was struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: Later he was removed for cruel excess.

literal: Xuanzu's son Fu, styled Xian-guang, was native-prefecture vice-governor.
idiomatic: Xuanzu's son Fu, styled Xian-guang, was native vice-governor.

literal: Son Tong.
idiomatic: Son Tong.

literal: Tong, styled Shulun, stood eight feet, with a towering look, skilled in dealing with the world.
idiomatic: Tong, styled Shulun, stood eight feet tall, imposing, and skilled in affairs.

literal: In the Taihe era he began as regular attendant in Prince of Beihai Xiang's state.
idiomatic: In Taihe he began as regular attendant to Prince of Beihai Xiang.

literal: At the start of Xiping he rose in succession to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At Xiping he rose to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the time Xiangzhou inspector Xi Kangsheng levied the annual tax in lengths of seventy or eighty feet to win a reputation for caring for the public; the commandery suffered.
idiomatic: Inspector Xi Kangsheng levied annual dues in seventy- or eighty-foot lengths to seem public-spirited; the region groaned.

literal: Tong, from the year's salary, had the office supply long silk.
idiomatic: Tong used his salary to have the office supply long silk.

literal: Tong then impeached Kangsheng for levies beyond measure.
idiomatic: Tong impeached Kangsheng for excess levies.

literal: When the memorial reached court, an edict punished Kangsheng and also praised Tong's public merit.
idiomatic: The throne punished Kangsheng and praised Tong's public service.

literal: In Emperor Ming's time court discipline grew slack and many stole military merit.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming discipline slackened and many falsified military merit.

literal: Tong reviewed the Ministry of Personnel merit rolls and on inspection found more than three hundred who had stolen ranks.
idiomatic: Tong checked Personnel merit rolls and found over three hundred false claimants.

literal: He then memorialized:
idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial:

literal: I observe that Ministry of Personnel merit registers are largely altered, and when checked against the Central Army Qin records they still disagree.
idiomatic: Personnel merit registers are widely altered and still disagree with Central Army Qin records.

literal: I hold that though crimes were pardoned by grace, they still must be corrected in the registers.
idiomatic: Though crimes were pardoned, the registers still need correction.

literal: Please send one chief clerk and one secretariat aide each from the Left and Right Vice Directors to gather Personnel and Central Army merit registers and check them line by line against memorial cases.
idiomatic: Send one chief clerk and one aide from each Vice Director to collate Personnel and Central Army rolls against memorial cases.

literal: Where name and rank match, at once write the rank count in large characters on yellow plain silk and have the bureau director stamp it in vermilion.
idiomatic: Where name and rank match, write ranks in large script on yellow silk and have the bureau director vermilion-stamp it.

literal: Clearly make two copies—one to Personnel, one kept at the Army bureau—to be held against the memorial case.
idiomatic: Make two clear copies—one for Personnel, one for the Army bureau—to match the memorial case.

literal: Going forward blocks erasure fraud; going back leaves no ground to alter.
idiomatic: Going forward blocks erasures; going back blocks alterations.

literal: From old times merit books sent up listed only names, not original commands.
idiomatic: Merit books sent up listed only names, not original commands.

literal: Hence thieves of merit treated the matter lightly.
idiomatic: Hence merit thieves grew bold.

literal: Now I ask that commoners in service list their native province, commandery, county, and ward head;
idiomatic: Now ask commoners in service to list province, commandery, county, and ward;

literal: those with real official posts should also list office, bureau, and service record.
idiomatic: real officials should list office, bureau, and service record.

literal: All should bear the native army's seal above, then seal the seam and send each to its superior.
idiomatic: All should bear the native army seal, then seam-seal and send up.

literal: Commanding generals and area commanders should all seal, then list up to the Mobile Secretariat.
idiomatic: Commanders and area commanders should seal, then send to the Mobile Secretariat.

literal: The Mobile Secretariat passes it to the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: The Mobile Secretariat forwards to the Grand Commandant.

literal: The Grand Commandant examines for truth, and only then passes it to the Secretariat.
idiomatic: The Grand Commandant verifies truth, then passes to the Secretariat.

literal: The Secretariat weighs it closely, then memorializes.
idiomatic: The Secretariat reviews closely, then memorializes.

literal: On the day the memorial issues, yellow silk with vermilion seal is sent to Personnel.
idiomatic: When the memorial issues, stamped yellow silk goes to Personnel.

literal: Recently it has not been only stealing ranks and false names or altering merit registers—some take one rank twice, or change names to receive grades; such men are not few.
idiomatic: Lately men steal ranks, swap names, or take one grade twice—not a few.

literal: Truly because Personnel lacks law and the barriers fail.
idiomatic: Personnel lacks law and the barriers fail.

literal: Why?
idiomatic: Why?

literal: After Personnel adds a rank the register is not annotated; for this reason opportunism is easy.
idiomatic: After ranks are added the register is not noted, so fraud is easy.

literal: From now on, after ranks are granted the name register should fully note them, add the date, have the director stamp, then hand to the bureau; the bureau director should make a separate copy handed on at each transfer.
idiomatic: After each grant, note name, date, and director stamp, then hand to the bureau with a copied roster at each transfer.

literal: Once this rule operates, fraud will largely cease.
idiomatic: This rule would largely stop fraud.

literal: An edict followed his proposal.
idiomatic: The throne accepted.

literal: Tong again memorialized:
idiomatic: Tong memorialized again:

literal: Your servant reflects that yellow-silk merit registers can only roughly stop fraud in the registers; fraud in the army is not yet ended.
idiomatic: Yellow-silk registers only roughly stop register fraud; army fraud remains.

literal: From now on, on the day army registers are reviewed, Mobile Secretariat, army secretariat, supervising army, and area commander should each keep clear documents and record everywhere.
idiomatic: On review day, Mobile Secretariat, army secretariat, supervisor, and commander should each keep records.

literal: For one rank from beheaded heads or more, issue a warrant at once.
idiomatic: One rank from heads or more gets a warrant at once.

literal: The warrant, on one sheet, should have in large characters at the center the Mobile Secretariat and commanding general's titles and the merit-holder's name.
idiomatic: The warrant should center the Mobile Secretariat and commander titles and the merit-holder's name in large script.

literal: For three slain rebels or wounds earning a rank or more, also write it on the warrant, each on one line, with a vertical tear down the center.
idiomatic: Three rebels slain or wounds earning rank should each get a line on the warrant, torn vertically down the center.

literal: The warrant should front and back bear reign era, month, day, the battle broken, the officer and merit, and seals as proof.
idiomatic: Front and back should bear era, date, battle, officer, merit, and seals.

literal: One copy to the merit-holder, one to the Mobile Secretariat.
idiomatic: One copy to the holder, one to the Mobile Secretariat.

literal: On reaching the capital it goes to the Gate Department for separate keeping.
idiomatic: At the capital it goes to the Gate Department for filing.

literal: Since the move of the capital, campaigns have often won; merit grants multiplied and could not all be entered—long years bred fraud, piled years bred falsehood, clever clerks climbed by links, and theft grew extreme.
idiomatic: Since the capital moved, victories multiplied merit grants beyond entry—years bred fraud and clever clerks stole ranks.

literal: From now, for all merit registers already memorialized and rewarded, broadly announce to far and near that such-and-such merit was judged, so all may know.
idiomatic: Announce every judged merit register far and near so all may know.

literal: Set a standard for reward with a three-year limit.
idiomatic: Set rewards on a three-year limit.

literal: Commoners in service and those entering office should all be ranked out within the limit;
idiomatic: Commoners and entrants should be ranked out within the limit;

literal: real offices and external titles should be granted by talent.
idiomatic: real offices and external titles by talent.

literal: Thus reward for toil would be quick, the effective encouraged, affairs not long delayed, and opportunism easy to end.
idiomatic: Reward would be swift, workers encouraged, and opportunism curbed.

literal: Or if hardship leaves a province without a Rectifier, that is outside this rule.
idiomatic: Provinces without a Rectifier in hardship are excepted.

literal: Also, showing merit registers should happen on the day of return from campaign.
idiomatic: Merit registers should be shown on return day.

literal: Yet recently Mobile Secretariat commanders and generals only draft them on reaching the capital, or after one or two years only then send merit books up.
idiomatic: Lately commanders draft only at the capital, or send books up a year or two late.

literal: The root of fraud truly lies here.
idiomatic: That is the root of fraud.

literal: Henceforth, on the army's return day pass merit registers at once; no delay past a month.
idiomatic: On return, pass registers at once—no delay past a month.

literal: An edict again followed his plan.
idiomatic: The throne accepted again.

literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Xiangzhou inspector Prince of Zhongshan Xi raised troops at Ye.
idiomatic: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, Xiangzhou inspector, rose at Ye.

literal: He was defeated.
idiomatic: Xi was defeated.

literal: Cha made Tong concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant and consolation commissioner and had him execute Xi in the province.
idiomatic: Cha sent Tong as Yellow Gate Attendant to console the province and execute Xi there.

literal: On return he was made regular Yellow Gate Attendant.
idiomatic: He returned and became regular Yellow Gate Attendant.
